content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecast shows gradual upward trend, but true values often dip sharply or show volatility after initial days.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward spikes in true values (e.g., 70s drop after 80s peak).
- Overshoots occur after large historical spikes (e.g., 85+ → forecast jumps to 78+ but true drops to 70s).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects downward after high historical values.
- Forecast lags true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the window, then catches up.
- Model ignores recent volatility in true values, especially after 75–80 range.
- Forecast assumes smooth trend, but true values show abrupt reversals or “jumps” in 3–5 day windows.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price drops after spikes (e.g., 80 → 70, forecast 78 → 76).
- Forecast tends to overestimate the “recovery” phase after dips, missing the true volatility.
